title: Practice in illness
hook: when the body can't, the practice can be lying down: Julian of Norwich's showings came on a sickbed
tomorrow: Job's friends got one thing right. what was it?

segments.voice: Yesterday, busy seasons: smaller, not stopped. Brother Lawrence turned the cake in the pan for love of God. Today the body can't even get to the kitchen.
screen: `SMALLER, NOT STOPPED.` → `THE BODY CAN'T GET UP.`

segments.voice: A fever. A phone face down on the blanket. A to-do list going stale on the table. Julian of Norwich, an Englishwoman, knew that bed. She writes that she was so sick the people around her thought she was dying. A curate came and set a cross before her face. She could barely move. And there, lying down, the showings came: visions she kept thinking and writing about long after.
screen: `A FEVER AND A STALE TO-DO LIST.` → `SO SICK THEY THOUGHT SHE WAS DYING.` → `A CROSS BEFORE HER FACE.` → `THE SHOWINGS CAME.`

segments.voice: What did they say? Many things, about love, about God's nearness. One line came while she was asking why God hadn't kept sin from the world, the sin that causes so much pain. The answer she heard, in Grace Warrack's old translation: "all shall be well, and all shall be well, and all manner of thing shall be well." She didn't receive it kneeling in a chapel. She received it in bed, unable to lift herself. That's a real piece of Christian teaching, older than Julian: the sick are not shut out of prayer. The letter of James says, "Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him." The sick person doesn't go to the prayer. The prayer comes to the bed. Churches still carry communion to people who can't come, and pray over the sick at home. So in Christian practice, an illness isn't a pause from the spiritual life. For Julian it was where the spiritual life happened. A rule can hold that too: an illness version, with no posture, no minutes and no notebook. Just you, lying down, and a line you can say without moving.
screen: `WHY SIN, WHY PAIN?` · `ALL SHALL BE WELL.` · `THE PRAYER COMES TO THE BED.` · `AN ILLNESS VERSION OF THE RULE.` · then, large: `LYING DOWN COUNTS.`

segments.voice: If you can, lie down or lean all the way back, and let the floor or the bed hold your whole weight. Rest your hands where they fall. Choose the one line your illness version would be, and let it ride on the breath until the bell.
Practice in illness: a version of your rule for the sick days, as small as a line said lying down, the way Julian's showings came on her sickbed.
Your line: lying down counts. Julian heard all shall be well in bed. Rest easy; that's day 1671.

screen: `DAY 1671 COUNTS.` → `WHEN IT BREAKS · 3 OF 12.` → `TOMORROW: JOB'S FRIENDS GOT ONE THING RIGHT. WHAT WAS IT?`

howItsDone: Churches bring communion to people who are sick at home and pray over the sick, following the letter of James. Christians who are ill still read Julian of Norwich's Revelations of Divine Love. On a personal rule, an illness version is a practice that can be done lying down.
